value: keep litter dry to limit ammonia buildup
avoid conditions and fast-growing breeds that increase risk

treatment_overview.value: No specific treatment described; management focuses on reducing litter moisture and overcrowding that cause the burns in the first place

summary.value: Hock burns are ammonia-caused skin lesions on the leg joints of chickens, common in overcrowded broiler operations with wet litter. They are not contagious but cause pain and mobility problems, and are used by welfare researchers as an indicator of poor housing conditions.
